title: Through Fire and Through Water
summary: God tests us because we need it, but he does not let our feet slip. He leads us through, and he works all things for our good.
exhortation: I grew up in a godly Christian household and in the church, so I shouldn't be surprised, but it still surprises me that God tests us. He puts things in our path that aren't easy and that we can't get around. We have to go through. The key is this: God tests us, but he doesn't let our feet slip.

We need to be tested. I have a 13-year-old son, and the other day he didn't want to go to a sports practice. I asked what he wanted to do instead, and he didn't really have an answer. I realized that if I didn't make him go, he'd probably just play video games. Maybe I should give him more credit, but I think we're all the same way. Given an easy path and a hard path, I'll pick the easy one every time. So God tests us because we need it.

There are probably things God protects us from that we'll never know about. But a lot of the time he says, "We're going straight through." I'm reading Genesis right now and seeing the choices of mankind. We chose sin. We chose rebellion. And God says, "I'm going to bring you through the choices you've made, but I will be with you and I won't let your feet slip."

Even with persistent sins, I've prayed, "Lord, why can't you just take this away?" And God says, "Because I want you to fight. My grace is sufficient for you. We're going through, and I'm going with you." When I slip into self-pity and think, "This will never go away. What's the point?", the point is that God is making us stronger. Our job is to fight, work hard and strive forward by the grace of God, and through it all he shows his steadfast love and faithfulness.

One of my favorite verses is Romans 8:28: "And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his purpose." Hold tight to that promise, Christian. God is working all things. Not most, not some, but all.
prayer: Lord, we thank you that you are a loving and kind Father. You know what is best for us. You lead us in paths of righteousness, not necessarily paths of ease, but through darkness, difficulty and trial.

And Jesus, thank you for what you have done, because you did not reject the hard path. You didn't look at the easy way and turn aside. You faced the hardest path there could be. You went straight to the cross, endured every bit of suffering and drank the cup of wrath for us. There is no harder path than the one you took. So we look to you, Jesus, the perfect man and our example. We trust you, we love you, and our hope is in you. Thank you, Lord. Amen.
